lines.text: She was in the last alcove. Smaller than the bed. Copper hair, gone dull, spread over the glass. Freckles on a face as white as frost.
Nell. Nell, it's me.
In her fist was a chip of glass, worn smooth at one end. The others never woke. Nell had woken. Just long enough, every so often, to draw a bird.
Gently. Lift the stone slowly. It has been drinking from her for four years. Pull it away too fast, and it may take the rest.
Tamsin lifted it the way you'd lift a sleeping bird off a nest. Nell's eyes opened. They found Tamsin's face, and stayed there.
Tamsin? You came. Did you get my birds?
Every single one.
Tamsin took out the little wooden bird she had carried for four years, and closed Nell's fingers around it.
I sent so many.
Then Nell saw Ash. Her eyes went very wide.
Is he going to eat me?
No. He likes you. That's worse. Now he'll follow you everywhere.
Tamsin made a sound that was half a laugh and half a sob. She had asked me those exact words once, in my square.
But Nell was so cold. Colder than the Skeld children in the Deep. Four years of pouring into stone, and her body had forgotten how to be warm.
Nell. I can keep you warm. But only if you'll have me. And I don't know how to give it back, once it's done.
She looked at Tamsin. Tamsin nodded. Nell looked back at me, and very slowly, she nodded too.
Yes.
I felt the thread go out of me, the way every thread always had. A line of cold, running from my chest into hers.
And then something came back along it. Warm. Like a small hand around mine on a winter night. For the first time since I left Greyhollow, I wasn't cold.
You're so cold. Here.
Lucan. That isn't how it works. It only ever goes one way.
I know.
Then, behind us, the stone that had lain on Nell's chest began to ring like a bell. And one by one, every stone in the farm began to answer it.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and one, coming soon.
